html:
An industrial accident on 10 July 1976 at a small chemical plant in Meda, about 20 km north of Milan in Lombardy, Italy. An overheated reactor released a cloud containing dioxin (TCDD), one of the most toxic substances known, over the town of Seveso and its neighbours.

The plant's owners were slow to say what had escaped. Thousands of animals died, and many children developed chloracne, a skin disease caused by dioxin. Hundreds of people were moved out of the worst zone and the topsoil was dug up. No one died at once, but the event left long fears about cancer and birth defects.

Seveso changed the law. In 1982 the European Community passed the Seveso Directive, which makes plants holding dangerous chemicals plan for accidents and tell the public. Later disasters such as Bhopal and Chernobyl kept the rules on the agenda.
